quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
Expect other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to the parked vehicles to give more room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep distance between your vehicle and parked vehicles. A person may step out of a parked car or walk between cars without looking. A driver may start moving their vehicle without seeing you.

questions.question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because a lane is ending ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Work zones have signs warning you about workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes. Reduce your speed and be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, what is the safest thing to do?

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than the other traffic.
Drive slower than the other traffic.
Drive at the same speed as the other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as the other traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other vehicles. Always drive at the same speed as traffic around you, but do not exceed the speed limit.

questions.question: What is the term for the amount of alcohol in your blood?

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC means a person is more impaired.

questions.question: Which statement about left turns is true?

options.text: You should swing wide into the right lane when turning left.
You cannot turn left from a two-way road at a red light.
When turning left onto a four-lane road, finish the turn in the far right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn left from a two-way road at a red light.
questions.explanation: You can only turn left at a red light when turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street. Always finish a left turn in the legal lane closest to where you came from.

questions.question: When you see a sign for your exit, what should you do?

options.text: Signal and move into the exit lane.
Slow down to the exit speed once you are in the deceleration lane.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: When you see your exit sign, start preparing. Signal and move into the exit lane. Once in the deceleration lane, slow down gradually until you reach the posted exit speed.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the road edge. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the road.
Speed up and steer back onto the road slowly.
Slam on the brakes and stop.
Gently apply the brakes to slow down. Turn the steering wheel to return to the road at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brakes to slow down. Turn the steering wheel to return to the road at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: If your wheels leave the road, keep driving on the shoulder and reduce speed by gently braking. When safe, turn the steering wheel to return to the road. Do not sharply jerk the steering wheel.

questions.question: A steady yellow light means the red light is coming. If you are already in the intersection, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Keep going and safely clear the intersection.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep going and safely clear the intersection.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, clear the intersection as quickly and safely as possible.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Even with rearview and outside mirrors, blind spots still exist. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger cars.

questions.question: How do you see vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Look in the inside rearview mirror.
Look in the outside rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. To check them, look over your shoulders.

questions.question: You cannot pass from either side of a ____ centerline.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no one can cross it to pass, no matter which direction they are driving.

questions.question: To avoid skidding on wet or slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. Braking while turning can cause you to skid.

questions.question: When it is raining or foggy, you should use your:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. Low beams help other drivers see you better.

questions.question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, you should look:

options.text: Only the left outside mirror.
Over your left or right shoulder.
Only the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Your mirrors cannot show your blind spots. Look over your shoulder to check the blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When you see a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.
Wait four seconds before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn. First, yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection, then turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle is using its siren and flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it has passed.
Stop immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Move to the right edge of the road and stop to let the emergency vehicle pass. Do not stop in an intersection. You can move again after it passes.

questions.question: When the road is wet and slippery, you should:

options.text: Avoid fast turns and stops while driving.
Test your tires' traction while going uphill.
Look less far ahead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid fast turns and stops while driving.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire grip. Drive slower and avoid sudden turns or stops to prevent skidding.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, you should:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.
Leave your transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels toward the curb when parking downhill. If your car rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: You should drive on the shoulder to pass another car:

options.text: If the vehicle ahead of you is turning left.
Never.
If the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you there and may pull onto the shoulder.

questions.question: When sharing the road with cyclists, you should:

options.text: Treat bicycles as vehicles on the road.
Be extra careful when driving near cyclists.
Leave plenty of space when turning after passing a cyclist.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Treat bicycles as vehicles with the same rights as cars. Drive carefully near cyclists and leave safe distance. Give plenty of room when turning after passing a cyclist.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder than daytime driving because you cannot see as well. It is harder to judge speed and distance. Stay farther behind the car in front of you. This gives you more time to stop if they brake suddenly. Use your headlights, but follow the rules about when to use high beams and low beams.

questions.question: As you drive, you're required to stop your vehicle:

options.text: At an intersection with a stop sign.
Where there is a red light.
When a traffic officer orders you to stop.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must stop your vehicle in these situations: at a stop sign, at a red light, or when a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you can check your blind spot by:

options.text: Using the inside rearview mirror.
Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
Using your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show all areas around your car. There are blind spots that mirrors cannot see. Before changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder to check these areas.

questions.question: A steady red arrow displayed on a traffic light means:

options.text: Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.
Drivers may turn in the indicated direction after coming to a complete stop.
Drivers may turn in the indicated direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means you cannot go in that direction. You must stop and wait for a green signal before you can proceed.

questions.question: The effect that alcohol has on your reflexes and judgment:

options.text: Is less pronounced when consuming beer instead of wine.
Is less pronounced when consuming wine instead of beer.
Is most pronounced when consuming hard ciders and mixed drinks.
Depends on the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: Depends on the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol can hurt your reflexes and judgment. The type of alcohol does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your blood matters.

questions.question: The best way to deal with tailgaters is to:

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater.
Slam on your brakes to get the other driver to back off.
Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage them to pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage them to pass.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors several times a minute to see if another car is too close behind you. If a car is tailgating you, slow down and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen when cars follow too closely.

questions.question: To let others know that you intend to turn, signal at least ____ feet from where you plan to turn.
questions.explanation: The law requires you to signal for at least 100 feet before you turn.

questions.question: When you see this yellow sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop at the crosswalk.
Stop at the crosswalk until a crossing guards signals for you to go.
Be prepared to stop if children are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop if children are in the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: This five-sided sign means you are near a school. Be alert and ready to stop if you see children in the crosswalk.

questions.question: A distraction when driving is:

options.text: Anything that causes evasive action while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your mind off driving. Distractions can happen anywhere and anytime. They can cause crashes that damage property, injure people, or cause death.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The highway ahead curves only to the right.
The highway ahead turns sharply to the right.
The highway ahead curves to the right and then to the left.
The highway ahead curves to the left and then to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highway ahead curves to the right and then to the left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They warn drivers about dangers ahead. This sign warns that the road curves right and then left.
